quote: 1. It's not supposed to be easy. Anyone who finds it easy is stupid.
speaker: Charlie Munger

quote: 2. There's nothing wrong with a forecast that turns out to be dead wrong. What's wrong is believing in it in the first place.
speaker: Howard Marks

quote: 3. Anyone who is not a millionaire but has one million in debt is a millionaire.

quote: 4. Be fearful when others are greedy and greedy when others are fearful.

quote: 5. It is not necessary to do extraordinary things to get extraordinary results.

quote: 6. The safest way to try to get what you want is to try to deserve what you want. It's such a simple idea.

quote: 7. You can't do the same things others do and expect to outperform.

quote: 8. All I want to know is where I'm going to die, so I'll never go there.

quote: 9. Rule number one: most things will prove to be cyclical. Rule number two: some of the greatest opportunities for gain and loss come when other people forget rule number one.

quote: 10. Anyone who doesn't possess shares should buy some; anyone who already has shares should hold on to them; and anyone who has neither shares nor money should sell his shirt and buy shares.

quote: 11. Markets are always wrong in the sense that they present a biased view of the future.

quote: 12. Money made on the stock exchange is like a loan – you have to give it back sooner or later.

quote: 13. It's far better to buy a wonderful company at a fair price than a fair company at a wonderful price.

quote: 14. It is remarkable how much long-term advantage people like us have gotten by trying to be consistently not stupid, instead of trying to be very intelligent.

quote: 18. My financial success stands in stark contrast with my ability to forecast events.

quote: 19. Rule No. 1: Never lose money. Rule No. 2: Never forget rule No. 1.

quote: 20. Should you find yourself in a chronically leaking boat, energy devoted to changing vessels is likely to be more productive than energy devoted to patching leaks.

quote: 21. He who understands, does not speculate; he who speculates, does not understand.

quote: 22. It takes 20 years to build a reputation and five minutes to ruin it.

quote: 23. If you're not willing to react with equanimity to a market price decline of 50% two or three times a century, you're not fit to be a common shareholder.

quote: 24. Never forget the six-foot-tall man who drowned crossing the stream that was five feet deep on average.

quote: 25. Diversification is protection against ignorance. It makes little sense if you know what you are doing.

quote: 26. When I see a bubble forming, I rush in to buy, adding fuel to the fire.

quote: 27. There are only two things that can happen on the stock market: it goes up, or it goes down.

quote: 28. Games are won by players who focus on the playing field – not by those whose eyes are glued to the scoreboard.

quote: 29. I made most of my money out of bear markets rather than bull markets.

quote: 30. Money is like soap: the more you touch it, the smaller it becomes.

quote: 31. Never invest in a business you cannot understand.

quote: 32. Only when the tide goes out do you discover who's been swimming naked.

quote: 33. Once we realize that imperfect understanding is the human condition there is no shame in being wrong, only in failing to correct our mistakes.

quote: 34. Time is the friend of the wonderful business, the enemy of the mediocre.

quote: 35. You don't have to be brilliant, only a little bit wiser than the other guys, on average, for a long, long time.

quote: 36. The riskiest thing in the world is the belief that there's no risk.

quote: 37. Chains of habit are too light to be felt until they are too heavy to be broken.

quote: 38. Well, I don't play the game by a particular set of rules; I look for changes in the rules of the game.

quote: 39. In my sixty years on the stock market, I have seen much more money disappear due to overreaction than disappear due to inflation.

quote: 40. Show me the incentive and I will show you the outcome.

quote: 41. Stock market bubbles don't grow out of thin air. They have a solid basis in reality, but reality as distorted by a misconception.

speaker: André Kostolany

quote: 44. Acknowledging what you don't know is the dawning of wisdom.

quote: 45. There is no logic in the stock exchange. That's the very reason why it's so interesting.

quote: 46. The difference between successful people and really successful people is that really successful people say no to almost everything.

quote: 49. Mimicking the herd invites regression to the mean.

quote: 50. I'm not much interested in the past history of a stock except as it tells me something about the possible reactions of people to future developments.

quote: 52. Do not save what is left after spending, but spend what is left after saving.

quote: 53. The financial markets generally are unpredictable.

quote: 54. Wherever I look, I see nothing but trouble ahead, but that is not a reason for gloom; it's a reason for being active and taking action.

quote: 55. It's not the validity of a belief that determines its influence but the intensity with which it is held.

quote: 56. Superior investors get that way because they have superior insight, not superior information.

quote: 57. You don't have to make it back the way that you lost it.

quote: 58. Never test the depth of the river with both feet.

quote: 59. Three rules for a career: Don't sell anything you wouldn't buy yourself. Don't work for anyone you don't respect and admire. Work only with people you enjoy.

quote: 60. If we avoid the losers, the winners will take care of themselves.

quote: 61. Someone is sitting in the shade today because someone planted a tree a long time ago.

quote: 62. I rely a great deal on animal instincts.

quote: 63. There's no investment idea so good that it can't be ruined by an excessively high purchase price.

quote: 64. Price is what you pay; value is what you get.

quote: 66. Being too far ahead of your time is indistinguishable from being wrong.

quote: 67. Only buy something that you'd be perfectly happy to hold if the market shut down for 10 years.

quote: 68. We may never know where we're going, but we'd better have a good sense of where we are.

quote: 69. The first rule of compounding: Never interrupt it unnecessarily.

quote: 73. Opportunities come infrequently. When it rains gold, put out the bucket, not the thimble.

quote: 75. You can't predict. You can prepare.

quote: 76. The most important quality for an investor is temperament, not intellect.

quote: 77. People calculate too much and think too little.

quote: 78. Risk means more things can happen than will happen.

quote: 79. Our favorite holding period is forever.

quote: 80. To the man with only a hammer, every problem looks like a nail.

quote: 81. If investing is entertaining, if you're having fun, you're probably not making any money. Good investing is boring.

quote: 82. Predicting rain doesn't count. Building arks does.

quote: 83. The big money is not in the buying and selling, but in the waiting.

quote: 84. It's not whether you're right or wrong that's important, but how much money you make when you're right and how much you lose when you're wrong.

quote: 85. Risk comes from not knowing what you're doing.

quote: 86. I think it's undeniably true that the human brain must work in models.

quote: 87. Those who have money can speculate; those who have a little money must not speculate; and those who have no money must speculate.

quote: 88. Beware the investment activity that produces applause; the great moves are usually greeted by yawns.

quote: 89. The desire to get rich fast is pretty dangerous.

quote: 90. Markets are constantly in a state of uncertainty and flux, and money is made by discounting the obvious and betting on the unexpected.
speaker: George Soros
